text:
ajay: noticing a spike in blackbox probe failures for streaming endpoints in us-west2 :eyes:
carla: same, started ~09:12 UTC, looks like TLS handshake errors in the logs
tom: can you paste a sample error?
ajay: logs show `alert: tls: unexpected handshake message` from our probe sidecar, repeatedly for different hosts
lina: we rotated certs for mTLS yesterday — could be ALPN or cipher mismatch during rollout :thinking_face:
maria: checking flow: are probes using http2/1.1? ALPN change could break streaming probes if they expect h2
ajay: probes are configured with `alpn: h2,http/1.1` in blackbox config, but infra-bot shows the control plane pushed `alpn: h2` only to a subset of pods at 09:10
probe-bot: automated note: 30/200 probes failing in us-west2 streaming group (streaming-check-v2).
carla: that partial push smells like a rollout race — some sidecars got new policy, others still accept http/1.1 so handshake mismatch for clients pinned to h2

lina: quick mitigation — relax probe ALPN to allow both during rotation, then re-enforce after all pods see new policy
ajay: +1. also reduce probe concurrency to avoid amplifying errors while we fix (we have ~500 probes every 15s currently)

maria: cost note: lowering from 15s -> 60s for streaming probes in that region reduces request bill by ~75% for that group; can revert after stable
tom: agree on rate reduction as temporary. Let's also tune Prometheus alert to avoid noisy paging: current alert fires on >5% failures over 5m which triggers for brief rollouts
carla: propose new alert: fail_rate > 10% over 10m OR sustained 3m breach in 3 consecutive windows. That suppresses transient rollout noise but catches real regressions

ajay: sample PromQL I used for local check:
```
100 * sum(increase(blackbox_probe_failures_total{region="us-west2",check="streaming"}[10m]))
/ sum(increase(blackbox_probe_runs_total{region="us-west2",check="streaming"}[10m]))
```
Use >10 threshold for alerting
lina: also add a log-based counter to pick up `tls: unexpected handshake message` specifically so we can break out mTLS/ALPN failures vs network timeouts

carla: runbook action items (quick):
- temporarily set probe ALPN to `h2,http/1.1` cluster-wide for streaming-check-v2 (apply with canary)
- throttle probe cadence in us-west2 to 1m
- update Grafana SLO dashboard to show probe fail-rate and TLS-specific error rate side-by-side
- postpone cert re-enforce job until all clusters have new policy

maria: I'll do the probe cadence change and ALPN canary, starting with canary pool-3 at 09:30 UTC
tom: I'll update the alert rule in prometheus-alerts (create a muted alert for the next 30m for this rule) and add the PromQL snippet to the dashboard

ajay: after we fix, we should run a canary job that verifies both ALPN modes for 10m to avoid this class of regression
carla: +1. longer term: add a pre-rotation probe in CI that simulates mTLS rotations (ALPN, cipher suites) against a staging gateway
lina: also adding a note to the SLO slack channel with a short summary and guidance for oncall to avoid escalations during cert rotations

probe-bot: automated note: canary rollout applied to pool-3 at 09:31 UTC, 3/20 sidecars updated
maria: canary looks good so far, no new handshake errors in pool-3 logs
ajay: rolling to pool-4 now, will watch dashboards (ping me if fail rate >8%)

tom: updated alert rule and muted historical noise. pushed dashboard panel with TLS-specific error series and probe cadence overlay
carla: thanks all — holding off on cert re-enforce job until EOD to give teams time to confirm stability :thumbsup:
ajay: closing loop: after 45m we reverted cadence back to 15s, ALPN remains permissive until next maintenance window. I'll file an infra-issue for the CI pre-rotation probe

maria: creating the ticket now and linking runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/probes-mtls-alpn

ajay: noted cost savings from the temporary cadence change in billing dashboard (~$320/day saved for this probe group) — we should add cost as a knob in runbook next time
carla: good cleanup. I'll post summary in #sre-weekly. :rotating_light:
